card.name: Event words after adverse or hypersensitivity
card.fires_on: The word right after a reaction-type noun, such as "events" after adverse or "reactions" after previous hypersensitivity, in warning text. It also fires on verbs like occurred, may develop, or emerge that follow a named symptom.

modes.label: Reactions after hypersensitivity
modes.description: The word "reactions" after "previous hypersensitivity" in the pre-treatment antibiotic allergy inquiry.
modes.example: it is important to inquire about previous hypersensitivity<< reactions>> to penicillins, cephal

modes.label: Events after adverse
modes.description: The word "events" after "adverse" in spontaneous report statements about withdrawal.
modes.example: there have been spontaneous reports of adverse<< events>> indicative of withdrawal and physical dependence occurring upon

modes.label: Verb after a symptom
modes.description: A verb such as occurred, may, or emerge that follows a named event or symptom.
modes.example: Infusion-related reactions were defined as any event reported to have<< occurred>> within 24 hours after the start

card.writes: Promotes words like "explicit" and "arisen", and suppresses runs of whitespace, so it pushes toward a continuation that elaborates on the event.
card.plain: It marks the spot just after a side-effect or allergy term where the label goes on to say when or in whom it happened.
